Subject: PO acknowledgement format + MSA exceptions for Ariba onboarding

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for kicking off the onboarding work. We are finalizing our Ariba registration and ran into two items that need alignment before procurement can finish the vendor setup: 

1) MSA redlines: our legal team flagged a couple of exceptions (liability cap language and a data residency carve-out). Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to accept the limited carve-out for EU customer data in the Order Form? We can surface the precise clauses if that helps.

2) PO acknowledgement & invoice mapping: our AP system requires a specific PO acknowledgment XML that includes a PO-level tax block and explicit ShipTo/InvoiceTo GL mapping. Can you share Redwood's accepted PO schema or a sample acknowledgement?

I attached a sample PO from our system for reference. We'd like to run a canary PO to validate the field mappings once you confirm the schema.

Appreciate a quick reply—our cutover window is June 10.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement
Acme Freight & Logistics

Subject: Re: PO acknowledgement format + MSA exceptions for Ariba onboarding

Hi all,

I reviewed the MSA redline packet (thanks Samir). Short summary from legal: 

1) Liability cap: we can accept a modestly elevated liability cap tied to direct damages only, provided there is an indemnity carve-out for data breaches caused by Redwood. We will propose language that narrows the categories of consequential damages.

2) Data residency: we cannot agree to a blanket EU-data-residency requirement in the MSA because our hosted model routing sometimes spans regions. We can accept an Order Form–level commitment for customer-specific data residency (i.e., for customers who purchase a dedicated/private deployment). For hosted accounts, we can offer contractual guarantees around encryption, access controls, and audit logs.

Recommendation: convert the residency ask into an Order Form checkbox/field (deployment type + region) rather than changing the MSA. That keeps the core MSA consistent.

Procurement/engineering notes needed from our side to validate the PO sample:
- Laura: confirm whether our PO acknowledgement supports an explicit tax block and multiple ShipTo/InvoiceTo IDs. If not, we should map the fields and provide transformation guidance.
- Also need to validate invoice workflow in Ariba (Invoice-to-PO matching tolerance, allowed line-item adjustments).

I attached a draft redline summary for the Order Form that implements the residency checkbox approach (vendor_msa_redline_v2.docx). Please treat as internal until we finalize language.

Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vendor_msa_redline_v2.docx (docx)
From: Samir Patel <spatel@acme-freight.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO acknowledgement format + MSA exceptions for Ariba onboarding

Thanks Rishi — that approach sounds reasonable. We prefer a solution that keeps the MSA stable and lets the Order Form capture deployment-specific residency commitments.

We ran the sample PO past our AP team — they confirmed the XML has the tax block and ShipTo/InvoiceTo nodes. I attached the sample again for clarity. We can schedule the canary PO for Thursday (June 4) if Redwood can produce the acknowledgement schema and a small mapping guide by Wednesday EOD.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood will accept a PO with an explicit net-45 payment term (we typically issue net-30 but the business is asking for net-45 on first 90 days to help cashflow)?

Samir
